source.title: Language Model Circuits Are Sparse in the Neuron Basis
source.authors: Aryaman Arora; Zheng-Xuan Wu; Jacob Steinhardt; Sarah Schwettmann

record.tranche_reason: The study compares neuron-basis and SAE-basis circuits in language models and finds that MLP activation neurons can produce similarly sparse, faithful circuits. This refines the inference that LLM circuit analysis requires features outside the neuron basis; it does not test superposition geometry itself.
record.gate_note: The paper reports circuit sparsity and faithfulness comparisons, not whether features overlap geometrically, how many features are represented per dimension, or whether an SAE dictionary recovers a complete canonical feature set. Cited results and statements about SAE splitting or absorption are not new results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study compares how many nodes a circuit needs for good faithfulness and completeness on subject-verb agreement (SVA). It does this across neuron and SAE bases and across attribution methods (IG vs. RelP), in Llama 3.1 8B and Gemma-2 2B/9B. Circuit size at a given faithfulness is a different construct from any version. It does not measure whether features overlap as near-orthogonal directions, how many features each neuron or dimension carries, what causes polysemanticity, or whether SAEs recover a complete, canonical feature set. A ~200-neuron circuit does not show those neurons are monosemantic or that features are not spread across neurons. The paper argues against the belief that the neuron basis is uninterpretable for circuits, but tests no superposition version. Its main comparisons pit its own pipeline (MLP activations + RelP) against other bases and IG. The finding is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a V4 verdict.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with qualifications. The authors conclude that circuit tracing on MLP activations matches SAE circuits at equivalent sparsity, and that neuron circuits reproduce CLT case-study findings (multi-hop capitals, addition, multilingual antonyms) plus new user-modelling results. Parity with SAEs requires their RelP attribution; under IG, neurons remain somewhat less sparse than SAE features. They attribute the sparsity to MLP activations being a privileged basis.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares circuit-tracing bases and attribution methods in language models; it does not reproduce the toy-model superposition method or measure feature-vector geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Circuit results vary with representation basis, attribution method, and paired versus unpaired SVA data; RelP generally improves on IG.

fits_no_version.finding: On SVA, circuits built from pre-down-projection MLP activation neurons reach faithfulness/completeness comparable to SAE-feature circuits at similar node counts. With RelP, about 200 neurons give near-perfect faithfulness. This holds across Llama 3.1 8B and Gemma-2 2B/9B, and SAE width barely changes SAE circuit sparsity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task circuits in LLMs are about as sparse in the MLP-activation neuron basis as in SAE dictionary bases (circuit sparsity of neuron vs. dictionary bases).

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The main circuit-size comparisons are largely presented in figures; the text gives only selected qualitative statements and a few approximate comparisons. The SVA circuit results do not directly measure feature distribution or representational geometry.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; the retained rows cover the reported SVA basis comparisons relevant to V4. Other attribution-method benchmarks and circuit steering case studies do not measure the representation-basis claim.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity transitions or feature geometry.
All: no capacity or feature-importance analysis.
All: no analysis of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
Whether features are spread across many neurons and whether SAEs recover sparse features. Circuit-node counts do not measure either.
Completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features. Only SAE circuit sparsity is compared, and SAE drawbacks are cited, not measured.
All: dimensionality of features is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T5/tests classification and V4 limits_scope label are not supported: no row measures feature distribution or superposition. Appendix F.1 neuron descriptions qualitatively show neurons responding to mixed contexts (e.g. English 'it' and Russian nouns), but no polysemanticity rate is reported. The MIB benchmark (Table 3) and the steering case studies are own-method evaluations, rightly left out. Statements about SAE error terms, splitting and absorption are cited from other work.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, sparse-feature superposition, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, and the causes of polysemanticity.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure or whether they indicate superposition.
The study evaluates sparse circuit bases in language models, not the distribution of individual semantic features across neurons or whether SAEs recover those features.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Whether the underlying features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Llama 3.1 8B base model
rows.operation_detail: Compared circuit size versus faithfulness and completeness across representation bases using Integrated Gradients.
rows.measure: Circuit size at comparable faithfulness and completeness
rows.value: MLP activations yield significantly smaller circuits than MLP outputs, by a factor of 100×; they also significantly close the gap with SAEs.
rows.note: The comparison is over four SVA tasks averaged together; the text gives the 100× comparison but not a specific circuit size or faithfulness/completeness values.
rows.check: Measures circuit size at comparable faithfulness/completeness (MLP activations ~100× smaller than MLP outputs under IG). It does not measure whether features are distributed across neurons or whether SAEs recover sparse features, so it cannot show V4's effect. The text also says IG neuron circuits remain somewhat less sparse than SAE ones.

rows.subject: Llama 3.1 8B base model
rows.operation_detail: Compared circuit size versus faithfulness and completeness for neuron and SAE bases using RelP and Integrated Gradients.
rows.value: With RelP, MLP activation performance reaches near-perfect faithfulness and completeness with only ∼ 200 neurons; the authors say RelP closes the gap between MLP neuron sparsity and SAE sparsity.
rows.note: The comparison is averaged over the four SVA tasks; exact plotted values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: Mainly compares the study's own attribution method (RelP) against IG. Only the reported ~200-neuron result is a basis comparison. It is a circuit-sparsity measure, not a measure of feature distribution or superposition.

rows.subject: Llama 3.1 8B base model
rows.operation_detail: Compared circuit size versus faithfulness and completeness for neuron and SAE bases on unpaired data.
rows.baseline: Other tested representation bases and Integrated Gradients
rows.value: The MLP activation neuron basis requires a considerably smaller circuit than other methods to achieve good faithfulness and completeness; RelP requires fewer neurons than IG.
rows.note: The appendix also says the overall pattern holds under zero ablation; no exact values are stated in the text.
rows.check: Unpaired-data replication of circuit-size comparisons, partly a RelP-vs-IG own-method comparison. It does not measure any version's construct.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Compared circuit sparsity and faithfulness/completeness across MLP activation, MLP output, and SAE bases.
rows.measure: Circuit size at comparable faithfulness and completeness
rows.value: MLP activations reduce circuit size by approximately 100x compared to MLP outputs at comparable faithfulness and completeness; the authors say they substantially close the gap with 16k SAEs and remain competitive against 65k SAEs.
rows.note: The text reports averaged results and qualitative comparisons; no exact plotted values are stated.
rows.check: Gemma-2-2B circuit-size comparison across bases. This is circuit sparsity, not feature distribution across neurons or SAE recovery of features. The appendix also states SAE width does not significantly affect circuit sparsity.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9B
rows.operation_detail: Compared circuit sparsity and faithfulness/completeness across MLP activation, MLP output, and SAE bases.
rows.measure: Circuit size at comparable faithfulness and completeness
rows.value: MLP activations provide substantially sparser circuits than MLP outputs while remaining competitive with SAE-based representations.
rows.note: The text reports qualitative comparisons, not exact plotted values.
rows.check: Gemma-2-9B circuit-size comparison. Same construct mismatch as R4, and only qualitative statements are given.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SVA circuit tracing in Llama 3.1 8B and Gemma-2-2B/9B
reader_labels.reason: The reported results show that neuron-basis circuits can be comparably sparse and faithful to SAE-basis circuits, so these circuit comparisons do not establish that useful LLM representations must be spread across neurons; see R1–R5.
